exam: What is the primary hormone that initiates phase III of the MMC? — Motilin, released during fasting, triggers high‑amplitude contractions.
A patient with chronic abdominal pain and weight loss has low serum motilin. What is the most likely diagnosis? — Motilin deficiency, often due to enteric neuropathy or chronic infection.
During a ward round, a patient shows dilated small bowel loops on X‑ray. Which investigation would best confirm MMC dysfunction? — Manometry to detect absent phase III contractions.
Why is a motilin antagonist contraindicated in a patient with chronic constipation? — It would suppress MMC, worsening stasis.
Which tropical infection is known to damage enteric nerves and impair MMC? — Schistosomiasis, especially S. mansoni.
A patient with TB presents with bloating and malabsorption. What first step should you take regarding MMC? — Treat TB aggressively to restore enteric function and motility.
ai.title: Initiation of the Migrating Motor Complex
ai.subject: Physiology
ai.summary: The migrating motor complex (MMC) is a cyclic, coordinated contraction pattern that clears the gut during fasting. Motilin released from the small intestine triggers phase II and III of the MMC, sweeping residual contents toward the colon.

sections.p: The MMC is a physiological rhythm that occurs every 90–120 minutes during fasting, preventing bacterial overgrowth and maintaining gut motility. It is essential for healthy digestion and is often disrupted in gastrointestinal disorders.

b: Motilin release peaks at 2–3 h after a meal
Receptor activation leads to phase III contractions
Contractions propel contents toward the ileocecal valve
sections.p: Motilin binds to receptors on smooth muscle cells in the small intestine, increasing intracellular calcium and generating coordinated contractions that propagate from the duodenum to the ileum.

t.b: Assesses MMC activity – low in motilin deficiency, high during fasting

b: Circadian rhythm aligns MMC with sleep cycles
sections.p: MMC is governed by neural (enteric), hormonal (motilin), and circadian mechanisms. Fasting, vagal tone, and gut microbiota influence its timing and strength.

sections.p: Disruption of MMC leads to stasis, bacterial overgrowth, and symptoms such as bloating, nausea, and malabsorption. Causes include motilin deficiency, enteric neuropathy, and infections.

sections.p: In low‑resource settings, MMC dysfunction may present as chronic abdominal pain or failure to thrive. Management focuses on treating underlying infections and supporting motility.
